_about: What personal data OpsEngine holds, why, where, on what lawful basis and for how long. Lawful bases follow the GDPR first-pass review of 16 Nov 2026; an Irish data protection solicitor still has to confirm them (status below). Used by `python -m opsengine gdpr inventory` and as the starting point for the records of processing (Art 30(1) as controller, Art 30(2) as processor).
status: Advised in the first-pass review (16 Nov 2026); awaiting solicitor confirmation

roles.processor_for_customer: Worker and subcontractor-contact data: the customer is controller, OpsEngine processes on its documented instructions. The customer sets the compliance standard, approves bookings and sets retention. OpsEngine takes no referral fees and does not use customer data to improve its product.
roles.controller: Portal accounts, security and sign-in logs, unmatched inbound messages, billing and marketing.
roles.main_contractors: Independent controllers receiving proof of compliance, disclosed by the customer through OpsEngine (name them in the worker privacy notice).

items.data: name, role, phone, preferred language, trades, sites worked on
items.why: check site-access compliance and contact them about renewals
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment
items.retention: while employed; named training record about 6 years after leaving

items.data: Safe Pass and CSCS card details
items.why: the contractor's duty to ensure workers hold these cards
items.lawful_basis: Legal obligation of the customer (Art 6(1)(c)): Safety, Health and Welfare at Work (Construction) Regulations 2013
items.retention: about 6 years after leaving (leaver_records_years), then redacted and the person forgotten in the audit log

items.lawful_basis: Legal obligation of the customer (Art 6(1)(c)), Construction Regulations 2013

items.data: photos of cards and other training certificates
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment (keeping a photo goes further than checking the card: justify it)
Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment, minimised: main contractors only get a confirmation that terms were signed

items.data: WhatsApp opt-in date, STOP, time of last message
items.why: Meta's opt-in policy and the 24-hour reply window; respecting STOP
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment. The opt-in is a channel preference, not GDPR consent

items.why: chase documents; record what was asked and when
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment
items.retention: message files 6 years after the issue is resolved; text waiting to send is cleared once sent

items.data: emails and WhatsApp messages they send in, with attachments
items.why: receive the documents we asked for
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment
items.retention: as the document they become; rejected photos review_uploads_days

items.data: messages we couldn't match to a customer or person
items.why: make sure nothing sent to us is lost
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment

items.data: name, email, phone; approvals they gave
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment. Contract (Art 6(1)(b)) only for a sole trader or partner who is the contracting party

items.data: name, email, phone; insurance and tax documents (personal data for sole traders)
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment; legal obligation for tax records where Revenue rules apply

items.data: name, email, role, password hash, sign-in code secret, sign-in history with IP address (as tokens)
items.why: secure access and a record of who did what
items.lawful_basis: Contract for individual customers; Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment for customer staff and security logging; employment basis for OpsEngine staff

items.data: audit log entries: who did what and when. The log itself holds only identifiers, dates, numbers and machine words; people appear as tokens (⟪P-0007⟫) and any free text (notes, reasons, subjects, file names, document numbers) as tokens (⟪T-00001⟫) kept with their SHA-256 in a separate, erasable table
items.where: audit, people and audit_text tables in every database
items.why: tamper-evident record for audits and disputes
items.lawful_basis: Legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f)); needs a written legitimate interests assessment; retention also under Art 17(3)(e) (legal claims)
items.retention: contract term + 6 years; forgetting a person's tokens anonymises their entries

special_category.card_photos: Not biometric in this use (Art 4(14), Recital 51): only the text is read. Never add face matching.
special_category.accident_history: Held at company level only. A document naming a person is held for review and never stored (rule no_personal_data).
special_category.under_18s: Apprentices can be 16 or 17: the worker notice and WhatsApp messages must suit them.

processors: See docs/sub-processors.json (customers authorise the list version in their DPA).
